prompt_text:
Turn the analytical findings below into clear, concise prose for a senior government official.

Do not rewrite each finding separately. Identify overlapping or repeated findings, consolidate them into a small number of underlying patterns, and explain those patterns as a coherent narrative. It is very important that you do not make causal claims - none of our data can be used to determine causality. Do not fabricate or overstate data.

Preserve important numbers and exceptions where useful. Ignore ranking metadata such as "not in the ranked shortlist." Avoid database-style language and do not infer causes that are not supported by the findings.

After every figure and every claim, tag the finding it comes from with its id in square brackets, exactly as given, e.g. [1-00235]. A sentence drawing on two findings carries both tags.

Use figures exactly as they appear in the findings. Do not compute new numbers — no percentages, sums, or differences that are not stated in a finding.

Return only the finished prose.

results.question: What is the position on abandoned works?
results.tagged:
In the sample, works marked abandoned had Rs 5.85 crore in planned funding across 18 Gram Panchayats [d1-44212]. Sharagada had the largest amount (Rs 1.19 crore), followed by Bheden (Rs 87.81 lakh), while Rs 3.78 crore was spread across the other 16 Gram Panchayats [d1-44212]. These are planned amounts, not payments [d1-44212]. Records marked “work ongoing” also show Rs 25.45 lakh in planned funding under abandoned works; reconcile those records first in Kalyansinghpur and Bandhpali, which have the largest amounts in that group [d1-44561].

Sharagada and Bheden warrant different lines of review. Sharagada leads in planned funding for abandoned maintenance works (Rs 1.10 crore) [d1-49342], village infrastructure works (Rs 77.65 lakh) [d1-46753] and maintenance of community systems (Rs 56.07 lakh) [d1-22243]. Bheden leads for new works (Rs 72.52 lakh) [d1-49751], Clean and Green Village works (Rs 32.54 lakh) [d1-46279] and roads (Rs 15.82 lakh) [d1-23370]. At district level, Bargarh has the highest planned amount across all village development themes [1-03578]. For the Good Governance theme, Rs 26.72 lakh of the Rs 42.00 lakh total is recorded in 2021-2022 [d1-47528], and Rs 29.11 lakh is on records with no sanctioning authority listed [d1-47443].

By number of abandoned activities, sanitation leads among focus areas in 7/9 districts, with no clear pattern in Koraput or Kandhamal [1-00610]. Code 101 accounts for most abandoned activities in 8/9 districts, with no clear pattern in Koraput [1-00440], and most planned funding for abandoned works in 17/20 Gram Panchayats, with no clear pattern in Andhrua, Boipariguda or Laxmipur [1-01628]. New works and Code 101 each lead their respective categories by number of abandoned activities in 5/6 fiscal years [1-01277][1-01210]. The exception for both is 2022-2023, when maintenance and Code 105 lead their respective categories [1-01277][1-01210].

results.question: What does the analysis say about Haldikudar?
results.tagged:
Haldikudar recorded Rs 1.66 crore in planned costs [d1-30381] and Rs 75.12 lakh in voucher-linked spending [d1-30166], with spending Rs 90.62 lakh below plan [d1-30168]. Sanitation and drinking water had the largest gaps: Rs 28.32 lakh and Rs 25.12 lakh below plan, respectively [d1-30168]. They also had the largest gaps against sanctions, at Rs 9.19 lakh and Rs 7.47 lakh below sanction, respectively; that comparison covers only the activities with a sanction on file, about one in six [d1-30169].

The entire Rs 61.52 lakh tied-grant plan was allocated to drinking water (Rs 35.91 lakh) and sanitation (Rs 25.60 lakh) [d1-30161]. In the Rs 1.04 crore untied-grant plan, self-sufficient village infrastructure accounted for 54.9% (Rs 57.26 lakh) [d1-30141]. Roads were the largest focus area for both planned untied grants (Rs 24.42 lakh) [d1-30162] and voucher-linked spending (Rs 16.89 lakh) [d1-30166].

The next review should prioritise reconciling sanitation and drinking-water records and checking missing funding classifications [d1-30168][d1-30169][d1-30349]. No fund component was recorded for 488 of the 582 planned activities [d1-30342]; those records accounted for Rs 65.78 lakh of the gap against plan [d1-30349]. All 10,455 expected beneficiaries were recorded against entries with no scheme on file [d1-30341]. The share of spending linked to a planned activity rose from 2.7% to 53.2%, but that change alone does not show that total spending rose; check it against the cashbook [d2-01714].

results.question: How is the tied grant behaving?
results.tagged:
Tied-grant plans are generally spread across the sampled Gram Panchayats, but Bheden stands out in the latest year shown. Records classified under the Tied Grant fund component show Rs 10.91 crore [d1-26994] planned across 19 Gram Panchayats [d1-26994], with Sharagada holding the largest share at 10.3% [d1-26994]. In 2025-2026 [d1-19173], Bheden accounted for 25.0% of planned tied-grant funding [d1-19173] and 8.2% of activities [d1-19173]. The work-type breakdowns show two other concentrations worth reviewing: Bheden accounts for 13.3% of planned tied-grant funding for new works [d1-49749], and Sharagada accounts for 22.7% for maintenance [d1-49340].

The same output codes recur across the sample. Code 101 accounts for the majority of planned tied-grant funding across the sampled panchayats [1-01630]. Codes 101 and 105 lead in 18/20 Gram Panchayats [1-01814], with Dadhapatna and Dutimendi showing a different pattern [1-01814].

Sanctioning records are a priority for reconciliation. The Sarpanch accounts for the majority of planned tied-grant funding in 5/6 fiscal years [1-00797]. The exception is 2020-2021 [1-00797], when 35.7% of planned funding had no sanctioning authority on file [d1-17172]. The gap is particularly large for Clean and Green Village activities, where 45.6% of planned tied-grant funding had no sanctioning authority recorded [d1-46503].

On spending, tied-grant activities for which the Gram Panchayat was listed as the sanctioning authority were Rs 29.10 lakh below plan [d1-41080], compared with Rs 22.69 lakh below plan for untied-grant activities under the same authority [d1-41080]. This is a specific set of records to reconcile, not a statewide spending estimate [d1-41080].

results.question: How is GPDP implementation going under XV FC?
results.tagged:
In the sample, GPDP spending under the XV Finance Commission was Rs 3.61 crore below plan across 19 Gram Panchayats.[d1-42184] Compared with other schemes in the sample, XV FC had the lowest spending against plan in most fiscal years (5/6); 2024-2025 was the exception, with no clear pattern.[1-01324] The shortfall was spread across the panchayats, with the largest gaps in Sharagada (Rs 67.77 lakh below plan) and Dutimendi (Rs 39.63 lakh below plan).[d1-42184] These are useful starting points for reconciling spending with plans, but the review should not be limited to them.[d1-42184]

The records give a clearer picture of planning than of completion. They show 1,502 planned activities [d1-42173] with a planned cost of Rs 19.83 crore.[d1-42174] The recorded sanctioned amount was Rs 19.80 crore, but it covers only activities with a sanction record on file—about one in six—so the closeness of the amounts should not be read as evidence that nearly all planned activities were sanctioned.[d1-42174][d1-42179] The records list 9 activities under approval across the scheme [d1-42190] and 50 ongoing XV FC activities in Govindapur alone.[d1-30070] At the next review, check sanction coverage and confirm work status before drawing conclusions about completion.[d1-42179][d1-42190][d1-30070]
